items.title: Search for 74-year-old doctor who went missing while windsurfing resumes
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A multi-agency search and rescue operation resumed today for a 74-year-old doctor who went missing while windsurfing off Tanjung Bungah yesterday, with seven boats and a helicopter deployed. The victim was reported missing near the Penang Chinese Swimming Club along Jalan Tanjung Tokong around 7.42pm yesterday. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the second day of the search operation, coordinated by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) would cover 94.76 square nautical miles.

items.title: Selgate opens first private hospital in Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Selgate Corp has expanded its presence in Selangor's private healthcare sector with the opening of its first private hospital in Sepang. Selgate group chief executive officer Noor Hisham Mohd Ghouth said the hospital's opening was part of the company's broader strategy to strengthen healthcare delivery and build an integrated healthcare ecosystem in Selangor. He said Selgate would continue to develop its hospital network and integrate services across its healthcare businesses.

items.title: Flood victims in Perak surge past 1,100 as waters rise again; Selangor sees slight relief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The number of flood victims in Perak has risen significantly to 1,110 people from 392 families this morning, compared to 191 people from 58 families yesterday evening, while Selangor has recorded a slight decrease. This is followed by the PPS at Dewan Orang Ramai (DOR) Sungai Relong (93 people), Masjid Ali Rouse Kampung Ulu Sepetang (91), Dewan Changkat Larah (73), SK Batu Hampar (71), DOR Kampung Simpang Halt (59), SK Matang Gelugor (58), Dewan Serbaguna Taman Kaya (56), SK Matang (49), Masjid Al Wusta (41), Masjid Al Hidayah (25) and DOR Air Kuning, Asam Kumbang (13). Meanwhile, in SELANGOR, 1,371 victims from 362 families remain sheltered at six PPS in the Kuala Selangor district this morning, compared to 1,399 people from 370 families yesterday evening.

items.title: Deepfakes, cyberattacks among five AI threats identified in Malaysia
items.summary: Organised by AI Malaysia as part of the development of the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030, the discussions highlighted the growing need for safeguards to ensure AI systems remain under human control. NAIO said the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030 recognised that regulatory oversight alone would not be sufficient to address emerging risks. "This approach is aligned with the human-centred AI principles underpinning AI Nation 2030.

items.title: Thai migrant smuggler held for threatening policeman with sickle
items.summary: PASIR MAS: A Thai migrant smuggler was arrested after threatening a policeman with a sickle during an operation at an oil palm plantation in Kubang Gadong last night. GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the operation was carried out by a task force following intelligence on the smuggling of undocumented migrants in the area. He said the team spotted a group of suspicious people during surveillance before two men, believed to be migrant smugglers, approached the personnel armed with a parang and a sickle.

items.title: Anwar races between Manila and KL as Asean meetings and Macron visit collide
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 16 — A series of summit meetings awaits Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on the third day of his visit to Manila today, before he makes a brief return to Malaysia this afternoon. However, Anwar is expected to return to Manila in the afternoon to attend the Asean-United States Special Summit and a dinner hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Today, Anwar is scheduled to attend the 29th Asean-China Summit, where he will deliver the Asean Common Statement on behalf of the bloc, as well as Malaysia’s national statement. He will also attend the 6th Asean-Australia Summit, the 16th Asean-United Nations Summit and the 27th Asean-Republic of Korea Summit, where he is scheduled to deliver Malaysia’s national statement at each meeting.

items.title: MRT Kajang Line resumes service after technical disruption
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Train services on the MRT Kajang Line resumed operations at 7.58am today following a technical disruption involving a train at Taman Suntex station. "Alternative train services activated to assist passengers during the disruption have also been discontinued," it said in a statement today. Rapid KL said train frequencies were being progressively adjusted to restore services in line with the scheduled timetable.

items.title: KEB makes flat start, dips slightly in ACE Market debut
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: KEB Bhd made a weak debut on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market on Monday, with its shares falling 7.1 per cent below their initial public offering (IPO) price within five minutes of trading amid subdued investor demand. At the prevailing price, KEB had a market capitalisation of about RM287 million. KEB's IPO raised RM48.49 million for the company through the issuance of new shares, while an offer for sale of existing shares generated RM30.88 million for the selling shareholders.

items.title: Three-vehicle collision on Senai-Desaru Expressway leaves two dead, two injured
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 16 — Two people were killed, and two others were injured in an accident involving three vehicles at Kilometre 52.5 of the Senai-Desaru Expressway (SDE), heading towards Desaru, early today. He said upon arrival, firefighters found that the accident involved a Proton X70, a Proton Persona and a Toyota Unser, with five people involved. Mohd Hazmi said two victims who were trapped in their vehicles were extricated using specialised hydraulic rescue equipment.

items.title: Australia, UK, Canada and Italy call on Israel to unblock Gaza aid
items.summary: LONDON: Australia, Britain, Canada and Italy on Sunday urged Israel to allow "rapid and unimpeded" humanitarian access to Gaza, calling the situation on the ground "dire." "We today urge the Government of Israel to stop the delays now and allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza," the countries said in a joint statement. "People in Gaza desperately need shelter and humanitarian assistance," the four countries said.

items.title: Bersatu seeks new strategy after Melaka election wipeout
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) needs an immediate strategic "game-changer" following its defeat in the Melaka election to turn its core Malay-Muslim support into seat victories, said its information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz. Tun Faisal said the party remained politically viable despite contesting without the advantages of federal or state government machinery. Official Election Commission (EC) results showed that Bersatu lost all seven seats it contested in the state election.

items.title: US Treasury chief demands answers from Nvidia over alleged China chip sales
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on Nvidia Sunday to explain whether it knowingly allowed its most advanced AI chips to reach China, saying this was more important than ex-CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged spy for Beijing. Speaking on "Fox News Sunday Morning Futures" three days after Huang resigned, Bessent said he wants to know if Nvidia used shell companies to dodge US restrictions and sell its most powerful chips to China. In late 2025, President Donald Trump did authorise sales of Nvidia chips called H200s to the Chinese – but not the most advanced chips used to run AI models reshaping modern society.

items.title: Fadhlina visits relief centre as floods affect 23 families in Nibong Tebal
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Nov 16 — A total of 23 families have been affected by floods in several areas of Sungai Kechil here, with some residents being housed at the Sungai Kechil MPKK Hall temporary relief centre (PPS) last night. Nibong Tebal Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the affected areas included Sungai Duri, Kampung Sethu, Kampung Besar, Kampung Sungai Buaya, Sungai Kechil and Jawi. She said that upon receiving information about the incident, she immediately went to the relief centre to assess the situation of the affected residents.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia opens lower as concerns over Nvidia continues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's key index opened lower on Monday, tracking Wall Street's weaker performance last Friday, as concerns over Nvidia's leadership uncertainty continued to weigh on market sentiment. At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) shed 6.89 points to 1,575.70 from Friday's close of 1,582.59. The benchmark index opened 6.69 points lower at 1,575.90.

items.title: Johor flags seven suspicious accounts spreading false information
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Johor government has lodged official complaints over seven suspicious social media accounts suspected of spreading false claims about state development projects and public facilities. Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the complaints sought investigations into the authenticity of the accounts, the content they circulated and the possibility of coordinated activity. The accounts also tagged Onn Hafiz and State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor in their posts.

items.title: China confirms first Xi-Trump-Putin summit on Thursday
items.summary: BEIJING: China confirmed that President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, will hold their first trilateral summit on Thursday in Shenzhen. "On November 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-US heads of state meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen," the foreign ministry said in a brief statement on Monday. German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said that in a recent meeting, Xi showed "irritation" when the idea of the trilateral talks covering Ukraine came up.

items.title: The 10 biggest stock market IPOs
items.summary: AgBank – US$19.2 billion. ICBC – US$19.1 billion. NTT Mobile – US$18.1 billion.

items.title: Man narrowly escapes as landslide hits home near Bagan Serai
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 16 — An elderly man escaped injury after a landslide and overflow of hill water affected his house at Jalan Bukit Merah, Kampung Bukit Merah, Simpang Empat Semanggol, near Bagan Serai in Kerian, last night. Perak Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call at 7.05pm, following which a team from the Bagan Serai Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene, 21 kilometres away. Sabarodzi said the operation was brought under control at 7.43pm and fully concluded at 8.20pm.

items.title: Pakatan needs new political realignment to win Putrajaya, says Amirudin
items.summary: KLANG, Nov 16 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) must focus its efforts on formulating a new political realignment as a strategy to form the government in the next general election, said PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. He said preliminary analysis had identified encouraging signs and a positive wave, including increased Malay support for PH in the Melaka state election, but its current performance was still insufficient to form a government without broader consensus. There has been some fairly positive growth for PH, particularly an increase in Malay votes.

items.title: Insight Analytics' Air Selangor win opens door to bigger water projects: analysts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Insight Analytics Bhd's entry into Peninsular Malaysia's water market through its first contract with Air Selangor could reduce its reliance on Sarawak projects and broaden its growth opportunities, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. Its analyst Walter Aw Lik Hsin said the RM3.2 million framework agreement with Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd marked an important milestone for Insight Analytics, as it was the company's first contract with the water utility and its first non-revenue water (NRW)-related project outside Sarawak. Beyond DMZ establishment, Insight Analytics could also venture into broader NRW management and water digitalisation solutions, potentially making Air Selangor a long-term growth avenue outside Sarawak.

items.title: Penang doctor disappears while windsurfing, search intensifies off Tanjung Bungah
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 16 — An elderly man has been reported missing while windsurfing in the waters off Tanjung Bungah, near a swimming club on Jalan Tanjung Tokong here last night. Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Fire and Rescue Operations Division assistant director John Sagun Francis said the victim has been identified as Dr Khaw Chun Sein, aged 74. A five-member team from the Bagan Jermal Fire and Rescue Station was then dispatched to the location.

items.title: Penang opens first relief centre as floods hit Sungai Bakap
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL: Penang opened its first temporary relief centre for the northeast monsoon transition last night after flash floods inundated two villages in Sungai Bakap. The evacuees were from Kampung Sungai Kechil and Kampung Sethu, which were inundated following continuous heavy rain. Based on data updated at 1.30am today, the evacuees comprised 23 adult men, 33 adult women, 19 boys, 13 girls, two baby boys and five baby girls.

items.title: Potential OPR hike to boost banks' NIM, Public Bank set to gain most
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A potential 25-basis-point (bps) hike in the overnight policy rate (OPR) in March 2027 could provide temporary relief to banks' net interest margin (NIM) pressure, said CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. Analyst Tan Ei Leen said Public Bank Bhd is expected to emerge as the biggest beneficiary, with an estimated NIM uplift of 4.0 bps in financial year 2027 (FY27). This is followed by Hong Leong Bank Bhd at 3.2bps, Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) at 2.6bps and RHB Bank Bhd at 2.3bps, based on the CIMB Securities' sensitivity analysis.

items.title: Malaysia won’t let US ties limit China engagement, says Anwar in Manila
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 16 — Malaysia’s relationship with the United States will not prevent it from engaging independently with other countries, including China, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said foreign investments must operate within Malaysia’s national policy framework and respect its interests, as the country navigates an increasingly uncertain geopolitical environment. Also present were the Prime Minister’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul and Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony.

items.title: Police arrest drug-positive man after knife scare at Kedah state government complex
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Nov 16 — Police arrested a man suspected of being under the influence of drugs when he attempted to trespass onto the grounds of Wisma Darul Aman here today, carrying a knife. Kota Setar district police chief ACP Syed Basri Syed Ali said police received information about the incident, which occurred at 8.10am, from a security assistant at the State Secretary’s Office. “The 45-year-old suspect rode a motorcycle through the entrance to Wisma Darul Aman without stopping at the security post.

items.title: Houthis push to within 60km of Aden as Yemen rushes reinforcements
items.summary: ADEN: Yemen's Houthis were advancing on the interim seat of the internationally recognised government on Sunday, positioned just 60km from Aden, sources told AFP, as government forces rushed to defend the city. Four military sources within government forces and two government sources said the Houthis had seized control of two districts in Lahj province and were moving towards Aden. Houthi military sources later confirmed that they had seized control of the Red Sea areas evacuated by government forces.

items.title: Presgo gateways proves intelligent integration drives true digital transformation
items.summary: For Presgo Gateways, winning the Outstanding Digital Transformation Project (Intelligent Parking) category at the PIKOM Digital Excellence Awards 2026 is less about the trophy and more about the real-world impact that preceded it: years of solving the operational challenges that keep cities running. The parking ecosystem now serves over 1.3 million registered users across 65,000 parking bays, processing approximately RM212 million in digital collections between 2016 and 2025. Beyond processing transactions, the platform supports around 100 on-ground enforcement officers with AI-assisted tools, optical character recognition, and vehicle recognition technology.

items.title: Macron: France looking to Malaysia to diversify rare earth supplies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: France aims to diversify its sources of rare earth supplies through cooperation with Malaysia. French President Emmanuel Macron said this was to reduce the risk of supply chain disruptions that could affect the country's factory operations and investments. He said this would be among the key focuses of his official visit to Malaysia, which also aims to strengthen economic partnerships and safeguard jobs and French industries.

items.title: 95 rescued after flash floods hit two Seberang Prai Selatan villages

John said the victims in Nibong Tebal comprised 32 adults (17 men and 15 women), 14 senior citizens (four men and 10 women), 22 children (11 boys and 11 girls) and three baby girls. "The victims comprised eight men, six women, three boys and seven girls.

items.title: Man with criminal record nabbed for driving cloned car, tests positive for syabu
items.summary: JELI: A man with a criminal record containing 13 entries was detained in Kampung Bukit Lakota yesterday after being found driving a cloned Honda Integra. District police chief Superintendent Kamarulzaman Harun said the 27-year-old was stopped by a police team on crime prevention patrol about noon. "The man was detained and the vehicle handed over to the Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department," he said, adding that the man also tested positive for syabu use.

items.title: Mystery over Batu Muda’s poor air quality deepens, DOE deploys drones and sensors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Department of Environment (DOE) is conducting drone surveillance and deploying additional air quality monitoring equipment to investigate the significant difference in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings between the Batu Muda and Cheras stations here. In a statement yesterday, the DOE said the measures were taken following API readings at the Batu Muda Air Quality Monitoring Station remaining at unhealthy levels of over 150 for the past two days, compared with the nearby Cheras station, which recorded readings of only around 60. “At the same time, drone-based air monitoring is also being conducted to help identify possible sources of air pollutant emissions, including open burning activities in the surrounding areas,” the statement said.

items.title: Two killed, two injured in three-vehicle crash on Senai-Desaru Expressway
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Two people were killed and two others injured in a crash involving three vehicles at Km52.5 of the Senai-Desaru Expressway (SDE), heading towards Desaru, early today. He said, upon arrival, firefighters found that the crash involved a Proton X70, a Proton Persona and a Toyota Unser, with five people involved. "Two others travelling in the Proton X70, aged 51 and 47, sustained injuries, while the driver of the Toyota Unser escaped unharmed," he said in a statement.

items.title: #NSTviral: Netizen wants DBKL to fix recurring Petaling Street rat infestation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A lasting solution is needed to address the recurring rat infestation in Petaling Street, where the problem has persisted despite repeated complaints and pest control efforts. In a post on Threads today, user @robinnsoon said the problem remained two months after their initial complaint was raised online. "Two months after my first post about the rat problem.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Proposed Nutrition Bill, crypto mining woes and rural EV access
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The proposed Nutrition Bill, illegal cryptocurrency mining and the expansion of electric vehicle (EV) charging station infrastructure are among the issues to be discussed in the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper published on Parliament’s official website, Rodziah Ismail (PH-Ampang) will ask the Health Minister during the oral question-and-answer session about the timeline for drafting the proposed Bill to regulate the nutritional intake of the public. The Dewan Rakyat sitting will then proceed with the tabling of the Finance Bill 2026 and the Measures for the Collection, Administration and Enforcement of Tax Bill 2026 by the Finance Minister for first reading.

items.title: Langgak Golf land rush: From RM7.8mil to RM193mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: In the rarefied world of Kuala Lumpur's luxury property market, few addresses command the prestige, privacy and exclusivity of Jalan Langgak Golf. But a landmark RM193 million bungalow sale has taken the value of prime residential land to an entirely new level. Occupying 92,835 sq ft of land, with a built-up area of 11,764 sq ft, the property fetched RM2,078.96 per sq ft (psf) based on land area.

items.title: Johnson & Johnson looking to buy Ollin Biosciences for up to US$3.4bil
items.summary: NEW YORK: Johnson & Johnson is poised to buy privately held eye disease drug developer Ollin Biosciences for up to US$3.4 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Under the terms of the deal being discussed, J&J could pay Ollin's backers US$2.2 billion upfront in cash and a further US$1.2 billion in potential milestone payments, the FT reported. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Nvidia allies plan 'war room' to push for Jensen Huang's return
items.summary: NEW YORK: Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive, and has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief's return and would try to garner support from the White House. "Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," the person said, adding that the efforts had Huang's support.

items.title: Ringgit opens almost flat against US dollar amid hawkish Fed outlook
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened almost flat against the US dollar on Monday as expectations of a further rate hike by the US Federal Reserve (Fed) continued to lend support to the greenback. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said higher US inflation expectations have reinforced the Fed's hawkish stance, with markets positioning for a rate hike in December and some pricing in a larger-than-usual move. "The US Dollar Index (DXY) continues to hover at an elevated level of around 103 points, while the 10-year US Treasury yield has stayed above five per cent.

items.title: China, US discuss tariffs, farm trade ahead of Xi-Trump meeting
items.summary: BEIJING: China and the United States discussed tariff cuts, agricultural trade and other issues at their first trade council meeting on Friday, China's Commerce Ministry said on Saturday, days ahead of an expected leaders' meeting in Shenzhen next week. "The two sides held candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges on implementing the outcomes of previous China-US economic and trade talks, including tariffs, a reciprocal 'US$30 billion-for-US$30 billion' tariff-cut arrangement, agricultural trade and other issues of mutual concern," the ministry said. Following a September summit between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump in Washington, the two sides proposed a US$60 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts, including roughly US$17 billion worth of US farm goods that China imported in 2024, but the plan has yet to be finalised.

items.title: AI safety must protect human lives and the human mind
items.summary: This is not an argument against artificial intelligence (AI). AI can bring real benefits to medicine, education, business, and public services. Second, laws must be able to address harm involving AI.

items.title: Intel sued by shareholders following 29pct stock plunge
items.summary: NEW YORK: Intel has been sued by shareholders who accused the US chipmaker of defrauding them by concealing the impact of a prolonged slowdown in personal computer sales that caused its stock price to plunge nearly 29 per cent in a single day. The shareholders said Intel's problems with PC sales and excess inventory outweighed data centre construction and other benefits related to the artificial intelligence boom. Shares of Intel closed Friday at US$59.66.

items.title: So, do you know what that Socso deduction in your payslip pays for?
items.summary: What is Socso? Socso administers several protection schemes, including the Employment Injury Scheme, Invalidity Scheme and the newer Non-Employment Injury Scheme, known as Lindung 24 Jam. Socso administers several protection schemes, including the Employment Injury Scheme, Invalidity Scheme and the newer Non-Employment Injury Scheme, known as Lindung 24 Jam.

items.title: From 328 to 56: Selangor flood hotspots down 82.9pc in 10 years, says MB
items.summary: KLANG, Nov 15 — The number of flood hotspots in Selangor has dropped significantly by 82.9 per cent, from 328 areas in the 2016/2017 period to just 56 locations this year, following the implementation of various mitigation measures as well as continuous improvement of the drainage system by the state government. “We will focus on the 56 identified hotspots because the efforts we have undertaken in Selangor have proven effective in reducing and addressing flooding, including in Kampung Bukit Lanchong and Taman Sri Muda in Shah Alam, as well as several other areas. Also present were Ministry of Education (MOE) Daily School Management Division director Mohd Hanafi Samad and Selangor Education director Wan Nor Ashikin Abu Kassim.

items.title: Woman dies in two-car collision near Kota Tinggi after vehicle veers into oncoming traffic
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 15 — A 60-year-old woman was killed in an accident involving two cars at Kilometre 45 of Jalan Johor Bahru-Mersing near Kota Tinggi today. Kota Tinggi district police chief Supt Yusof Othman said police received information from the public about the incident at 2 pm. He said the accident involved a Toyota Vios driven by a 33-year-old man and a Proton Saga driven by a 28-year-old woman.

items.title: Zahid: Negeri Sembilan royal dispute to be resolved soon, in line with state constitution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said the dispute involving the Negeri Sembilan royal and the state administration will be resolved soon in accordance with the state constitution. “We will do whatever necessary, provided that the problems faced by the people of Negeri are resolved and that the state administration runs smoothly and operates in accordance with the state constitution.” However, the state government officially withdrew that letter yesterday, reaffirming its commitment to uphold the state constitution and customary traditions.

items.title: ‘We won big’: Sanusi wants PAS-led Perikatan-BN partnership to carry on to GE16
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Nov 15 — PAS leader Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor today said Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) should carry their partnership into the 16th general election after their win in the Melaka state election. Sanusi, who is both PN and PAS election chief, said he hoped to see that happen after seeing how the majority of voters accepted the pairing, Berita Harian reported this evening. Asked about his lighter presence on the Melaka campaign trail, Muhammad Sanusi said he had to concentrate on preparing the state budget, which required close scrutiny.

items.title: Perikatan to decide stance on Sarawak polls as BN sits out, says Annuar Musa
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) will determine its stance on contesting the upcoming Sarawak state election soon, according to its Information Chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa. This follows an announcement by BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi that the coalition will not contest any seats in the 13th Sarawak state election. “BN has no intention of contesting any state seats in Sarawak, as this is the understanding between Umno and PBB in the state,” Zahid said.

items.title: GRS MPs to submit memorandum to PAC, seek expanded Pan Borneo probe
items.summary: PAPAR, Nov 15 — Seven Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) Members of Parliament will submit a memorandum to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) next week seeking an expanded scope of investigation into the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project, including an examination of the basis and implications of the decision to terminate the Project Delivery Partner (PDP) model in 2019. Papar MP Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. their spokesman, said the move was important to ensure that the PAC investigation not only focused on the project’s current status and performance, but also examined previous policy decisions allegedly affecting its implementation schedule, contractor appointments and rising construction costs.

items.title: With MIC’s backing, BN vows to field PPP candidates in upcoming general election, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is committed to fielding candidates from the People’s Progressive Party (PPP) to represent the coalition in the upcoming 16th General Election (GE16). BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan remained steadfast alongside other coalition partners in efforts to revitalise the party as a new component member of BN. “With the agreement of Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran (MIC president) and Datuk Seri M. Saravanan (MIC deputy president), I am determined that we will field PPP candidates in the upcoming general election,” he said in his speech at the Malaysia PPP Deepavali Open House here today.

items.title: Parit Yaani crash: Johor govt to bear medical costs, provide monthly aid to orphaned siblings, says exco
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Nov 15 — The Johor government, through the Johor State Islamic Religious Council (MAINJ), will cover the medical costs, including plastic surgery, for the two orphaned siblings who survived an accident along Jalan Yong Peng-Muar, near Parit Yaani, on November 1. State Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said the assistance would also include a monthly allowance, as both children were orphaned following the tragedy. Elaborating, Mohd Fared said the state government was also prepared to cover other expenses should the need arise.

items.title: Vehicles over 5m barred from Sibu road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang until Feb 28 for festive decor
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 15 — Vehicles exceeding five metres in height are prohibited from entering a designated road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang until Feb 28, 2027 to accommodate Christmas street lighting and festive decorations. Sibu Municipal Council (SMC) in a statement said the restriction, which took effect on November 14, applies to the road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang, behind the WTK Holdings Berhad building. Meanwhile, the council said the Sibu Christmas Celebration 2026, themed ‘Lighting Up Sibu, Celebrating Christmas Together’, aimed to bring the community together, promote cultural harmony and share the joy of the festive season.

items.title: Senator warns early Parliament dissolution could derail Budget 2027 and force temporary spending, citing 2022 precedent
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 15 — Calls for an early dissolution of the Dewan Rakyat are ill-timed as Budget 2027 has yet to complete the parliamentary approval process, said Senator Datuk Ahmad Ibrahim. He said dissolving Parliament before the Budget was passed could disrupt the government’s financial planning and delay funding for development projects, infrastructure programmes and other public commitments. “This would require a new government and Parliament to reintroduce and approve the Budget, potentially delaying financial authorisations needed to sustain government operations and implement planned programmes.

items.title: Kedah aims to cut operating deficit to 10.59pc with RM1.34b Budget 2027, says MB
items.summary: He said the revenue target represented an increase of RM12 million from the RM838 million targeted in 2026, with land revenue contributing the largest share at RM551 million, followed by miscellaneous revenue (RM253 million), forestry revenue (RM30 million) and district revenue (RM16 million). He said RM245 million of the development allocation was set aside for the State Development Fund, involving 10 implementing departments, while RM12.53 million was allocated for forestry development. The Water Supply Development Fund received RM143.75 million, comprising RM138.75 million from federal government loans for the implementation of three loan-funded projects and RM5 million from the state government’s allocation.

items.title: BN to skip Sarawak state polls under Umno-PBB understanding, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will not contest any seats in the 13th Sarawak state election, its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. The decision is in line with an understanding between Umno and Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said. Also present were PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan and MIC deputy president Datuk Seri M. Saravanan.

items.title: ‘Do not be alarmed’: MetMalaysia to conduct tsunami warning siren test in Kudat tomorrow
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 15 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) will conduct a siren test for the Malaysian Tsunami Early Warning System (SAATNM) at the Kudat District Police Headquarters (IPD) tomorrow. In a post on Facebook, MetMalaysia said the test is scheduled to take place between 9 am and noon. “MetMalaysia will provide updates should there be any changes,” the statement read.

items.title: Ageing 40-year-old water tank bursts in Kuala Kangsar, affecting 520 consumers; no damage or injuries reported
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 15 — The bursting of a 455-cubic-metre water tank at Taman Kuala Kangsar in Kuala Kangsar yesterday was caused by the condition of its structure, which was more than 40 years old. Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Public Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said the Kuala Kangsar operations centre of the Perak Water Board (LAP) received information about the incident at about 5pm, which affected water supply to approximately 520 consumers in the surrounding areas. He said LAP had carried out washing and cleaning works on roads around the burst Taman Kuala Kangsar tank, while direct water supply through the main pipeline to the affected areas, namely Taman Kuala Kangsar and Taman Meranti, had also been implemented.

items.title: Selangor flood evacuees fall to 1,399; Perak down to 191
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — The number of flood evacuees at temporary relief centres in Selangor and Perak declined as of 4pm today. In SELANGOR, 1,399 people from 370 families were still taking shelter at six relief centres in Kuala Selangor, down from 1,493 people from 398 families this morning. In PERAK, the number of evacuees also fell to 191 people from 58 families, compared with 293 people from 85 families this morning.

items.title: One hour of rain, roads under water: Flash floods hit Shah Alam’s i-City
items.summary: A user, frhn.jefx, posted a video showing a flooded road near i-City, with several vehicles, particularly motorcycles, forced to stop along the stretch. Another user, jacketpotato.sa, also shared information on conditions along the same route, showing several cars making their way through the floodwaters. Another user, charlie.kilo.maggi, shared footage of flash flooding at 2.46pm along the exit from the i-City area.

items.title: Seats, candidates, strategy — Sarawak DAP will decide, says Loke
items.summary: KLUANG, Nov 15 — DAP has given full autonomy to the Sarawak DAP leadership to decide how many seats to contest, who to field and its strategy for the upcoming Sarawak state election, party secretary-general Anthony Loke said. “All decisions concerning the Sarawak state election will be made by Sarawak DAP. Asked about the party’s seat projections and the challenges it would face in the state election, Loke said details would be announced by the Sarawak DAP leadership at an appropriate time.

items.title: From setbacks to comeback? Dzulkefly wants Amanah ready for GE16
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 15 — Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) must use its defeats in several state elections as a springboard to strengthen the party and prepare its machinery for the 16th General Election (GE16), its vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said. He said the entire party leadership and machinery, particularly the youth and young women, must self-reflect, strengthen the organisation and devise more effective strategies for reaching out to the people. Dzulkefly said Amanah’s struggle should not be centred solely on electoral victory; rather, political victory must serve as a means to build a united, strong and dignified nation-state grounded in the values of human dignity (karamah insaniah).
